title: Jesus catches Peter Part 2
scripture_text: ‘’One day as Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret, the people were crowding around him and listening to the word of God. He saw at the water’s edge two boats, left there by the fishermen, who were washing their nets. He got into one of the boats, the one belonging to Simon, and asked him to put out a little from shore. Then he sat down and taught the people from the boat. When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into deep water, and let down the nets for a catch.” Simon answered, “Master, we’ve worked hard all night and haven’t caught anything. But because you say so, I will let down the nets.” When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to break. So they signalled their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink. When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees and said, “Go away from me, Lord; I am a sinful man!” For he and all his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken, and so were James and John, the sons of Zebedee, Simon’s partners. Then Jesus said to Simon, “Don’t be afraid; from now on you will fish for people.’’ So they pulled their boats up on shore, left everything and followed him.’’
devotional:
At this time Peter got a revelation not only of Jesus, but also of himself.

He began to see himself as he had never seen himself before. He said to Jesus: “Go way from me Lord for I am a Sinful man.” It would be very easy to miss the full impact of what Peter is saying here, he is redefining himself. He is seeing himself as he really is, i.e. with the blinkers removed, the blind spots revealed. This was a moment of clarity and honesty; this was an unveiling of Peter’s heart and an acknowledgement of Jesus’ holiness. In this confession he is saying, I am unworthy to be in your presence, he is confessing his need of mercy and grace. He understands that sin produces distance between himself and God. Surely God wants nothing to do with a simple, sinful fisherman. It is best that Jesus go.

It is more necessary for us as Christians to experience the holiness of God than the power of God. There is something inside all of us that longs for a transforming experience of holiness. To be holy is to discover God’s original intention for our lives.

Peter got a new perspective on what was important in life. Luke tells us that Peter left everything and followed Jesus. He left his boat and nets, symbols of his security and identity. But he not only left his boats and nets, he left nets that were brimming with fish, he left a lucrative business, he left financial security. His leaving was a decisive break from all that was known, to pursue the unknown and the uncertain. The leaving everything meant that Peter’s whole value system changed, what was once important and essential for him became like discarded refuge on a beach.

The forth effect that this revelation had on Peter is probably the most noticeable if not the most radical, for it changed how Peter related to others; it increased Peter’s ability to relate to those who by culture and religious orientation where totally opposed to Peter and all that his religious heritage stood for.

If you read the rest in Luke 5 you will notice that Peter began to associate with people who he would never have associated with before. He met a paralysed man whom Jesus healed. In this culture the paralysed man would have been viewed as the worst kind of sinner and his illness seen as punishment for sin. Next Peter met Levi who was a chief tax-collector and seen as a traitor and collaborator with the oppressive Romans. Because Peter experienced the grace of God, he was able to move beyond his comfort zone and relate to people who at one time he would have hated and despised.
prayer: Father may I have an honest evaluation of myself so I can accept others
